active_paradigms.idea: Solve per-layer replica-count and GPU-placement choices jointly with SciPy HiGHS MILP
active_paradigms.description: The displayed adapter only returns the original evaluator's aggregate result, so its exact balance/time formula is not visible here; inspect that imported evaluator before choosing a solver cutoff. The current program first fixes node groups, then greedily chooses replica counts by largest current weight/count, and finally uses capacity-constrained LPT to assign already-fixed replicas to GPUs. This is fast and valid, but it cannot undo a poor replica decision when that decision creates an unbalanced GPU partition. For small and medium layer configurations, formulate one independent `scipy.optimize.milp` per layer with binary variables representing a choice of replica count k for each expert and assignment of its k copies to GPU slots. Precompute each copy's load as weight[e]/k, require exactly one k per expert, exactly k selected copy placements when k is selected, and exactly physical-experts-per-GPU copies on every GPU. Add a continuous makespan variable T and constraints that each GPU's selected copy-load sum is at most T; preserve the hierarchical policy by only allowing an expert's copies on GPUs belonging to its assigned node. Minimize T with a very small secondary linear term favoring fewer disruptive changes or deterministic slot order, then reconstruct `phy2log`, ranks, counts, and the padded inverse map exactly as required. Use this only below a conservative variable-count threshold and retain the current vectorized greedy method as fallback for large instances.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimizes maximum expected GPU expert load, which is the weakness of separate greedy replication and LPT placement; use it when evaluator balance gains outweigh solver runtime.
active_paradigms.cautions: The load contribution must be weight[e]/k for every selected copy, not weight[e], and rank values must be dense 0..k-1 per logical expert. MILP symmetry is substantial, so impose canonical copy ordering and a strict time limit; an untimed MILP can destroy the execution-time component or evaluator timeout. Do not use this if the evaluator requires a specific stable group ordering beyond node locality.

active_paradigms.idea: Replace greedy LPT GPU packing with a single min-cost-flow assignment over replica streams and convex GPU load tiers
active_paradigms.description: The current implementation's strongest feature is that replication allocation is cheap and mathematically equivalent to repeatedly choosing the largest weight/count stream. Its main placement weakness is that LPT decides each item against only the current least-loaded GPU, so it has no global view of which later heavy streams will compete for the same GPU. Keep the current group-to-node assignment and replica counts, because these preserve locality and make the output shape straightforward, but replace only the within-node physical-replica-to-GPU packing. Build a directed flow graph for each layer-node: every replica stream supplies one unit, every GPU has exactly its physical-expert capacity, and GPU capacity is represented by ordered unit-capacity tier arcs. Give replica-to-tier arcs costs based on a discretized convex overload penalty relative to the node's ideal total load, so expensive heavy assignments into already expensive tiers are discouraged. Solve the assignment in one call to `networkx.min_cost_flow`, decode each replica's GPU and position it within that GPU, and leave the existing logical rank/count reconstruction unchanged. This is globally optimized for the chosen convex surrogate rather than the myopic LPT objective and is especially useful when a few replicas remain much heavier than the rest.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce post-replication per-GPU load variance and maximum overload without changing the locality-preserving node/group and replica-count stages; potentially improve balance at moderate runtime cost.
active_paradigms.cautions: The flow graph must enforce one unit from every physical replica and exactly the required number of units into every GPU; otherwise it can silently leave slots unused. Costs should be bounded integer values because NetworkX min-cost flow is integer-cost based; scale float weights carefully and use deterministic tie breaking. This is slower than tensor LPT, so gate it to small per-node replica counts or only layers whose greedy predicted max load exceeds a threshold; never invoke it for every large layer blindly.

active_paradigms.idea: Use a one-shot Hungarian assignment against load-targeted GPU slots after replica allocation
active_paradigms.description: The existing final `balanced_packing` is a vectorized LPT heuristic: it is fast across layers but commits each descending replica to the currently lightest non-full pack. A distinct inexpensive alternative is to expand each GPU into its fixed number of physical-expert slots and solve a single rectangular assignment with `scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` separately for each layer-node. Construct a cost matrix between replica streams and GPU slots using the evaluator-relevant expected replica load and a static convex target penalty: slots on each GPU receive increasing marginal prices around the target node load, with deterministic tiny perturbations for ties. Calibrate the slot price curve from the total replicated load divided by GPUs, so assigning a heavy stream to a late/high-price slot is much more costly than assigning it to an early slot. Hungarian assignment globally chooses all stream-slot pairings under exact capacity, unlike sequential LPT, while its cubic complexity can remain acceptable for typical per-node expert counts. Decode slot index into GPU and local physical position, preserving the existing replica stream identities and `phyrank`. This is a good middle ground when MILP is too expensive but greedy LPT leaves measurable imbalance.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve the global quality of GPU-slot placement while retaining the current fast greedy replica allocation and exact GPU capacity constraints.
active_paradigms.cautions: A static assignment cost is a surrogate, not the exact squared load of a GPU, because actual GPU load couples all assigned streams; validate the target-price schedule against the real evaluator rather than assuming lower surrogate cost means a higher score. Ensure all slots are included exactly once and keep all assignments within their node when hierarchy is active. Hungarian is cubic in replicas per node and creates CPU arrays, so use it only when its measured runtime beats the score's runtime penalty, with current LPT as fallback.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve the per-layer replica-count and placement problem directly with a bounded mixed-integer linear program
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first greedily assigns whole logical groups to nodes, then greedily chooses replicas by largest current weight/count, and finally applies LPT packing to GPUs. This is fast and produces valid maps, but its three irreversible greedy stages optimize local proxies rather than the final maximum GPU load. Formulate a small per-layer MILP with binary assignment variables for physical slots, constraints that every logical expert has at least one replica, exactly `num_replicas` slots are filled, each GPU receives `num_replicas / num_gpus` slots, and replica rank/count consistency is maintained when emitting the maps. Add a continuous variable `T` and constrain each GPU's summed per-replica expected load to be at most `T`; if hierarchical locality is required by the original evaluator, restrict every expert's copies to the node selected for its group. Use the current greedy solution as an incumbent/warm start if supported, impose a strict small time limit, and retain the greedy result whenever the MILP does not prove or find an improvement quickly. This directly attacks the likely load-balance portion of the combined score rather than optimizing the intermediate group and replica proxies. The evaluator adapter only exposes `combined_score`, not its formula, so inspect the imported original evaluator before deciding whether node-load constraints must also be included in the MILP objective.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Final per-GPU maximum load and tail imbalance, while using a hard solve-time cutoff so improved balance does not lose more combined score through runtime.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A full binary formulation can be too large for all layers/configurations; apply it only below a variable-count threshold and fall back to the present vectorized greedy algorithm. The emitted `phy2log`, `phyrank`, `logcnt`, and padded `log2phy` must remain mutually consistent, including experts with only one copy. Do not optimize a fractional relaxation and round it without repair, because capacity and replica-count violations can invalidate evaluator results.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the final LPT GPU packing with a single min-cost-flow assignment using convex load-slot costs
tried_paradigms.description: The existing `balanced_packing` is capacity-constrained LPT: it sorts replicas by load and sends each next replica to the currently least-loaded non-full GPU. Its strength is deterministic speed, but it cannot reconsider early heavyweight placements and can be noticeably suboptimal when several replicas have similar large loads. Keep the existing group-to-node and replica-count stages, then build one flow network independently for each layer-node: each physical replica is one unit of supply, each GPU has exactly `phy_experts_per_gpu` position nodes, and all GPU positions feed the sink with unit capacity. Give the arc from replica `i` to the k-th position of GPU `g` a discretized marginal cost derived from a convex penalty around the target GPU load, with later positions on a GPU increasingly expensive. Run one `networkx.min_cost_flow` call to obtain a globally capacity-feasible assignment rather than sequential LPT decisions. Calibrate the marginal-cost scale from the actual replica loads and target total-load/number-of-GPUs, so the flow minimizes a close surrogate for squared overload or maximum-load excess. Convert the resulting selected replica-to-position arcs into the same `pphy2phy` permutation currently consumed by the map construction. This is structurally different from changing replication: it preserves valid counts but improves the last placement decision where the evaluator is most likely to observe imbalance.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: GPU-level load dispersion after replication, especially cases where LPT's earliest assignments create an avoidable overloaded GPU.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Flow costs must be nonnegative integers for reliable NetworkX min-cost flow use; scale floats conservatively and use deterministic rounding. The load-slot surrogate is not exactly a nonlinear makespan objective, so compare its predicted maximum load with LPT and keep LPT if flow is worse. Graph size grows with replicas times GPUs times slots, so use this only for moderate per-node instances or use a coarse set of load slots.

tried_paradigms.idea: Deduplicate exactly equal layer load vectors before rebalancing and expand the maps afterward
tried_paradigms.description: The current code vectorizes across layers but still performs every sort, greedy replica decision, and packing loop for every layer, even when workload collection contains repeated load histograms. Since all operations are deterministic functions of one row of `weight` and the topology parameters, identical rows necessarily have identical optimal greedy outputs. Before calling either hierarchy path, use `torch.unique(weight, dim=0, return_inverse=True)` to retain only distinct layer rows, run the existing high-quality algorithm once on that compact matrix, and index the three output tensors by `return_inverse` to restore original layer order. This preserves every output value exactly relative to the current program for duplicate rows, so it has no correctness or load-balance trade-off. It can substantially reduce wall time when many MoE layers share a routing distribution, are zero-load, or workload traces are repeated, which can improve the combined score even if the evaluator's balance metric is unchanged. Extend the same idea to an all-zero-row fast path if that is common, because any valid canonical placement is balance-equivalent for such rows. This exploits an important property the current batched implementation does not exploit: vectorization avoids Python overhead but does not avoid repeated algorithmic work.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Algorithm execution time with exactly unchanged expert placement quality for repeated rows; this is the lowest-risk way to improve a combined quality/runtime score.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Only exact equality is safe unless the evaluator explicitly tolerates approximate map changes; do not quantize or cluster near-equal weights. `torch.unique(dim=0)` may itself cost time and memory, so activate it only when the number of layers is sufficiently large or a cheap duplicate check indicates repetition. Preserve CPU device, integer dtypes, and inverse-index ordering when expanding `phy2log`, `log2phy`, and `logcnt`.
